# apps/outreach

The public site at opendatacapture.org: an Astro 5 marketing site plus the Starlight user manual,
built to `output: 'static'`. Nothing else in the monorepo imports it, and it is **not** part of
`pnpm dev` (that filters to api/gateway/web) — run it with `pnpm --filter @opendatacapture/outreach dev`,
which serves on `OUTREACH_DEV_SERVER_PORT` (4000).

Read the root `AGENTS.md` first for the rules that apply everywhere.

## The content in this package is a mirror. Do not edit it here.

Three paths under `src/content/` are **symlinks into the repo root**:

| Symlink                    | Real location |
| -------------------------- | ------------- |
| `src/content/blog`         | `/blog`       |
| `src/content/docs/en/docs` | `/docs/en`    |
| `src/content/docs/fr/docs` | `/docs/fr`    |

Editing a file through the mirror path writes to the repo-root file, but reviewers and the rest of
the repo refer to `/docs` and `/blog` — go there directly.

**Do not add an `AGENTS.md` or any other non-post Markdown file to `/blog`.** The `blog` collection
loads every `.md` under that symlink and validates it against the post schema, so an unrelated file
fails `astro check` with `InvalidContentEntryDataError`. Blog guidance lives in
`.agents/docs/playbooks/add-blog-post.md` for exactly this reason. `/docs` is not affected: the
symlinks point at `/docs/en` and `/docs/fr`, so `docs/AGENTS.md` sits outside both collections.

`src/plugins/astro-plugin-symlink.ts` exists because pnpm + Astro content collections do not follow
symlinks on their own. It monkey-patches the `astro:content-imports` Vite plugin: when Astro throws
`UnknownContentCollectionError` for a real path, the plugin rewrites the id back through the
`collections` map declared in `astro.config.ts` and retries. If you add another mirrored directory
you must register it there, and the mapping key is a path **inside** `src/content`, not just a
collection name.

MDX under `/docs` imports `@/components/...` and `@astrojs/starlight/components` even though those
files live outside this package. That works only because `astro.config.ts` aliases `@` and
`@astrojs/starlight` in `vite.resolve.alias`. Any other bare specifier imported from a doc will fail
to resolve.

## Docs structure

Every file in `/docs` carries an **explicit `slug` in frontmatter that includes the locale**
(`slug: en/docs/introduction/home`). The numeric filename prefixes control ordering only, never the
URL. French coverage is partial — only `docs/fr/1-introduction` exists.

The Starlight sidebar is not fully autogenerated: `astro.config.ts` lists one `autogenerate` group
per top-level directory (`docs/1-introduction` … `docs/6-updating` — Starlight strips the locale
segment). A new top-level section will not appear until you add a group there.

`src/content/docs/en/runtime-core-docs/` is **generated and gitignored**. `starlightTypeDocPlugin`
(`src/plugins/starlight-plugin-typedoc/`) regenerates it from `@opendatacapture/runtime-core`'s
`lib/index.d.ts` on every build, so hand edits are lost. To change that API reference, change
runtime-core's TSDoc. Background: `.agents/docs/architecture/runtime-and-vendor.md`.

## Content collections

Config is `src/content/config.ts` — the legacy Astro path, **not** `src/content.config.ts`. The
collections use the legacy API too: no `loader`, and entries expose `.slug` / `.render()`.

| Collection     | Type    | Notes                                                                                                                                                                   |
| -------------- | ------- | ----------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------- |
| `blog`         | content | `author` is `reference('team')` — the value must match a filename in `src/content/team`. Both languages live in one flat directory and pages filter on `data.language`. |
| `docs`         | content | `docsSchema()` from Starlight                                                                                                                                           |
| `faq`          | data    | YAML, `order` drives display                                                                                                                                            |
| `team`         | data    | YAML; `image` is `'@/assets/headshots/<name>.webp'` and is **refined to be square**                                                                                     |
| `testimonials` | data    | same square-image refinement                                                                                                                                            |

A non-square headshot fails the build with the refine message, not with an image error.

## Pages and i18n

Locale is a route parameter: everything user-facing lives under `src/pages/[locale]/`, and each page
needs `export const getStaticPaths = () => [{ params: { locale: 'en' } }, { params: { locale: 'fr' } }]`.
The exceptions are `src/pages/index.astro` (a bare meta-refresh to `/en/`), `src/pages/404.astro`
(Starlight's own 404 is disabled via `disable404Route`), and `src/pages/resources/**.json.ts` —
static JSON endpoints (runtime package metadata, instrument JSON Schemas) linked from the docs.

**i18n here is hand-rolled and has nothing to do with `useTranslation` from libui.** Use
`useTranslations(Astro.url)` from `@/i18n`, which derives the language from the first path segment
and returns `{ t, translatePath, resolvedLanguage, altLanguage, altURL }`. Keys are dotted paths into
`src/i18n/translations/*.json` and are typed by a mapped type, so a new namespace requires both the
JSON file and an entry in the `TRANSLATIONS` object in `src/i18n/index.ts`. There is no inline
`t({ en, fr })` form. Sort the JSON with `pnpm --filter @opendatacapture/outreach format:translations`.

## Styling

Tailwind v4 via `@tailwindcss/vite`. Two dark-mode attributes coexist: marketing pages use
`data-mode` (set inline by `src/scripts/theme-init.js`), Starlight uses `data-theme`, and
`src/scripts/theme-observer.js` — injected into Starlight's `<head>` from `astro.config.ts` —
syncs them. Style against `data-mode` outside of Starlight.

`cn` comes from the local `src/utils.ts`, which wraps clsx and tailwind-merge directly. That is
deliberate; the eslint ban on importing those two applies only to `apps/web` and
`packages/react-core`.

## No React, no tests

Every component is `.astro`; there are no React islands and no client framework integration
configured. Do not introduce one without asking.

There is **no `vitest.config.ts` and no test suite in this package** — `pnpm test` does not cover it.
`pnpm --filter @opendatacapture/outreach lint` runs `astro check && eslint --fix src`, and `astro check`
is the only thing type-checking `.astro` files, so run it after any change here.
